Trump said Friday that losses among Iran’s leadership have left him with nobody to talk to and predicted the war would end “very, very soon.”

CENTCOM said US forces helped Persian Gulf partners move more than 100 million barrels of crude through the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, while US operations have blocked at least $25 billion in Iranian oil exports and put pressure on government and IRGC finances.

Trump said earlier Friday that the US may strike Iran’s fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site “very soon,” while reiterating that Tehran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

EU leaders condemned Iran’s attacks in the region and called on Tehran and its proxies to refrain from further attacks and destabilizing activities. They also condemned threats to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran warned that Americans, US allies and military bases would be considered legitimate targets if Washington used unconventional weapons, including the Mother of All Bombs.

Iran has helped the Houthis target drone and missile attacks and provided training, intelligence and tactical guidance for attacks on Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people briefed on intelligence from Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s anti-Houthi alliance.

The support has contributed to a Houthi offensive that has made rapid territorial gains in Yemen, the Journal said.

The group now controls the coastline on its side of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and has attacked Saudi oil tankers, energy facilities and airports, including a strike in Riyadh last weekend that killed at least 13 people, the report added.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said Saturday that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 68 nautical miles northeast of Saudi Arabia’s Jubail on Friday.

All crew members were safe and had been evacuated, UKMTO said, adding that no environmental impact had been reported.

Damage to fuel storage tanks during the war reduced Iran’s reserves and left the country facing shortages in the second half of the year, the Environmental Protection Organization chief said on Saturday.

Shina Ansari warned that fuel shortages, combined with winter temperature inversions, would worsen air pollution.

Learn: Iran's acting Defense Minister Majid Ebn al-Reza said on Saturday that the “titles and dimensions” of bombs did not matter, arguing that Iran’s missile power had changed the balance and forced its adversaries to say, “Yes, sir!”

Exports through customs offices and border markets in Iran’s southeastern port city of Chabahar and nearby areas totaled $464.3 million in the first six months of the Iranian year (from March 21 to September 22), up 120% from the same period last year, the city’s customs director said.

They included $109.7 million in goods declared for export at Chabahar, Pishin and Rimdan, and $354.6 million in goods declared at other customs offices and shipped out through the Chabahar area, Reza Ghorbani said.

A woman was killed and five civilians, including another woman and a girl, were wounded in Houthi shelling and sniper fire in Sabir al-Mawadim district southeast of Taiz, the Taiz Human Rights Center said, according to Yemen’s state news agency Saba.

The center said the casualties included a woman wounded by a Houthi sniper and three brothers injured by shrapnel when a shell fired by Houthi forces struck their home. It called for an end to attacks on civilians and accountability for those responsible.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Baghdad on Saturday to attend the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s Council of Foreign Ministers, Iranian state media reported.

The meeting runs through Sunday and Araghchi is expected to hold bilateral meetings with other participating foreign ministers, according to the report.

100%Oct 17, 2026, 04:30 GMT+1Vitol star oil trader to leave after Iran war bet losses - WSJStar oil trader Yau Yau Lu is set to leave commodities giant Vitol by the end of the year after his team suffered several hundred million dollars in losses on a bet made at the start of the Iran war, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

Lu and his team took losses after betting the wrong way on diesel and crude prices, though some were quickly recovered, the report said.

One person familiar with the matter told the Journal that Lu was leaving Vitol for family reasons.

The report said several Vitol rivals, including Trafigura and the trading arms of BP and TotalEnergies, have profited from disruptions caused by the Iran war.

Vitol has not disclosed its financial results for the year, but a person familiar with the matter told the Journal in April that the company was up for the year despite Lu’s trades.

REUTERSOct 17, 2026, 03:38 GMT+1Israel sharing intelligence on Iran-backed Houthis with Saudi Arabia - KanIsrael has begun sharing intelligence on Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen with Saudi Arabia through the United States, Israel’s Kan public broadcaster reported, citing a Middle Eastern diplomat.

Kan reported Saudi Arabia requested US assistance and Washington passed the request to Israel, which began providing intelligence because it views the Houthis as a broader regional threat.

A foreign source familiar with the matter told Kan that US representatives who recently visited Israel said during talks in Cairo that Israel could provide Saudi Arabia with extensive intelligence based partly on the Israeli military’s experience confronting the Houthis.

The intelligence was primarily intended to help secure freedom of navigation through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, according to the report.

The discussions took place as Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo, where US Central Command representatives participated in security talks and proposed a joint regional mechanism to help Saudi Arabia confront the Houthis, Kan reported.
